The Purpose of Any Secret.

Let the secret be whatever it may. When you cannot make it known by letters and messengers to a friend living nearby or far away, summon one or two from the spirits of Iasguarim, appoint them as your couriers, and entrust the secret to them, doubting nothing.

Let the letters be formed at will.

This is the prophecy of Nicolaus Basselius of Irbus, S. Episc., which he saw in the Spirit. And he said: Thus says the Lord to the shepherds of the churches: Soon you will perish, because a very great calamity will scatter your broad dominion and will spatter all Europe. Woe to the Ishmaelites, who break the covenants of the tabernacle, because through envy and recklessness they seize the pastures. Behold, the dominion that you have will be broken unless you hasten to fuller repentance; and you will be handed over to be torn apart. Alas, the whole Church has been spattered with the worst morals; hypocrisy has invaded its ministers. Flee, do not look back; you will be laid waste, and you will be dragged by dogs; they will spatter the whole earth with blood. Seek repentance, inhabitants of the earth. Young Benjamin will experience disturbances. Woe to the inhabitants of Genesareth, which is Europe, because on account of the multitude of their sins they will perish under the hands of the Bulgarians. Here ends the prophecy of Nicol., bishop, [unclear], 12 Kalends of May.

When the person to whom they are sent has received any letters whatsoever marked beforehand with the sign of Iasguarim, let him, being skilled in the art, do everything prescribed according to the art, observe the order of the planets, and write what must be written. And when the conjuration written above has been said, as soon as the sent spirits have appeared, let him say to the first among them: Chamerusin othriel arnotiel solais elty. Naeles proy vear sato cralnoti, penason. When these words have been said, the spirit, at once approaching, will faithfully and calmly reveal the message entrusted to him.

Let the letters be formed at pleasure.

This is the prophecy of Nicolaus Basselius, Bishop of Irbuia, which he saw in the Spirit. And he said: Thus says the Lord to the shepherds of the churches: Soon you will perish, because a very great calamity will scatter your broad dominion and will besprinkle all Europe. Woe to the Ishmaelites, who break the treaties of the tabernacle, because through envy and rashness they seize the pastures. Behold, the dominion that you have will be broken, unless you quickly show greater patience; you will be handed over to be torn apart. This whole Church has been besprinkled with the worst morals; pretense has prevailed among its ministers. Flee, do not look back; you will be laid waste, and that region will be dragged by dogs; they will besprinkle the whole earth with blood. You seek the patience of the inhabitants of the earth. Little Benjamin will experience disturbances. Woe to the inhabitants of Gennesaret, which is Europe, because on account of the multitude of their sins they will perish beneath the hands of the Bulgarians. Here ends the prophet Nicolaus, bishop. 12 Kalends of May.

When the one to whom they are sent, being skilled in the art, has received letters of whatever kind marked beforehand with the sign of Lasguarim, let him do everything that is prescribed according to the art, and let him observe the order of the planets and write what must be written. And when the conjuration written above has been spoken, immediately, when the spirits sent have appeared, let him say to the first among them: Chamerusin othriel atnotiel solais elty. Naeles proy veat fato cralnoti, penafon. When these words have been spoken, the spirit, approaching at once, will faithfully and peaceably reveal the message entrusted to him.

CHAPTER

THE SECOND BOOK.

CHAPTER XXIII.

Whose hour is called Aalacho, and whose supreme angel is called Emperor Dardariel; he has under his command dukes, counts, and many spirits.

The eleventh hour of the night is called Aalacho, and its supreme emperor of spirits is called Dardariel, having under his command many most powerful princes and dukes, who preside over counts and almost infinite ministerial spirits. These dukes are exceedingly benevolent, cheerful, and pleasant, and they delight in associating with human beings; and they are most obedient to those operators who have been well instructed in the art. And note that the number of these dukes is infinite, because the air, once penetrated, is filled with them, and they cannot be counted. Solomon Hermes says, and we have experienced, that among the dukes, counts, and ministerial spirits of Dardariel there are many good, useful, and most honorable spirits, who always desire to benefit human beings, always exhorting them by a certain invisible teaching toward the good, toward honorableness, peace, concord, integrity of faith, love of God, observance of his commandments, contempt of the world, desire for supreme blessedness, and every good. These are good and most holy spirits, who love, venerate, and possess God, who delight to be with holy and God-fearing human beings, because they have been appointed by God, the Creator of all things, as their protectors.

Others, however, are evil and most pestilential apostates from God, enemies of all good things, who continually tempt mortals and lie in wait for human beings. And whatever the good spirits establish for the honor of God, these always strive to destroy and revoke. The air is full of these malignant spirits; they run and roam invisibly among human beings, always inciting them to evil, and they drag the unwary with them to hell. Through these evil spirits of Dardariel there are countless acts of sorcery, not only among Christians but also among unbelievers; and they especially deceive petty women more ready for malice. And whoever wishes to devote himself to acts of sorcery through them will be, in evil things, powerful above all other sorcerers and worthy of eternal fire. But we, who seek to teach not evil but good...

THE SECOND BOOK.

Our Lord Jesus Christ, the most gentle savior of our souls, promised us the happiness of eternal consolation, if we always observe his commandments with a pure heart. Therefore, dearest brother, carefully keep the commandments of God and of the holy rule, because unless you preserve inviolate until death all the things that almighty God has commanded you, you will perish by eternal death. For this reason I have handed down to you the form and law of religious and holy conduct. Take care, then, diligently, lest through the desire of love you give your heart to any mortal creature to possess, because no one comes to those highest joys unless he despises the world for God’s sake. Therefore again through this letter of mine I exhort you, as a dearest friend, to observe for yourself the admonitions I have made. For I consider myself happy when I have written something good, especially at this time, for edification concerning the manner of living well, by which you may always become better. For this reason I now write to you again for your good, because I fear your danger no less than my own. But I pray: always be watchful, advancing daily in the fear of God, living innocently, harming no one, and persevering entirely in a holy purpose. Do not put your trust in time, fortune, or age, because they are nothing, unless we are. Truly I love you sincerely in Christ Jesus, praying that he himself may arrange that I also am beloved by you, and that although I am absent from you in body, I may always be present in spirit. Therefore, since I continually remember you in my prayers, I earnestly beg you not to forget me. Farewell. The twelfth day before the Kalends of May, in the year 1500.

CHAPTER XXIV.

WHOSE HOUR IS CALLED XEPHAN, AND its supreme angel and emperor is called Sarandiel, having under him princes, leaders, counts, and many servants.

The twelfth hour of the night, which borders on dawn, is called Xephan, and its angel is named Sarandiel. He has under his command many spirits, good and bad: princes, leaders, counts, and ministerials, who are appointed to various operations, the good to good things and the bad to bad things. These princes, as Hermes the Hebrew, who is called Solomon, says in the fourth book On the Offices of Spirits, often appear in the form in which the Devil is read to have appeared to Eve, having one beautiful head like that of a maiden, with hair hanging down on both sides,

but two serpentine bodies, which nevertheless they always veil and hide beneath certain coverings or leaves, so that they may not be seen. In face, however, they are very beautiful, benevolent, and pleasant, and most ready and cheerful for every obedience to the operator.

When you see the spirits standing before you in a strange form, let them not frighten you, because they are good and benevolent, harming no one; and, lest they terrify anyone, they almost always hide their monstrous form, appearing with a very beautiful face. O wretched man, and truly pitiable, why do you not attend to the instability of all temporal things? And why do you not think that you will die soon? Remember what the first man deserved because he violated the commandment. Would that, as Balaam wished, our soul might die the death of the righteous, so that, despising present pleasures and the vain honors of the world, we may be immaculate, keeping ourselves from every sin. But we do not care, until at last the dreadful bonds of death fall upon us forever. I consider that man happy who has thought these things beforehand [unclear]

The Second Book.

137

... keeps these things in mind. Therefore, O man, cast away the world, as the Son of God did, and consider what evils pursue us from love of it. For it brings many dangers upon us; and since it is damnable to its lovers, it is rightly despised. Truly the lover of the world is worthy of eternal death. What profit is that world to you, miserable man? When it is loved, it flees; while it is present, it passes away; when it raises up, it casts down; when it flatters, it deceives; when it blooms, it withers; when it sends forth its lovers, it sends them on to everlasting miseries. In the year 1512, on the Kalends of May.

When the letters have been received and the sign of the principal Spirit recognized, let one skilled in the art do what is customarily to be done. Then, when the conjuration written above has been spoken according to the art, the Spirits will appear, faithfully revealing what was entrusted to them.

Chapter XXV

In which we shall teach the general manner and form of approaching this art of Steganography, and of operating in it without danger and with the greatest usefulness.

Whoever desires to approach the hidden knowledge of this art of ours, whoever wishes to work marvels through it, useful to many dangers, must first be adorned with virtues, with a clean conscience and good will toward God, himself, and his neighbor, so that he is not inclined to harm anyone, nor seeks dealings of baseness. Next, he must necessarily be somewhat imbued with the good literary arts, and especially with the science of the stars, so that he knows the general motions, courses, movements, changes, orders, natures, positions, risings, settings, and effects of the stars, signs, and planets; for without competent knowledge of these things no one can have access to the depths of this art. Consequently, he must have a teacher perfect and experienced in the art, because we believe it possible to come to this knowledge without a teacher only for a few, and those most learned in many things, and especially skilled in magical matters. The teacher, however, must be not only proven and experienced in knowledge, but also faithful; for the purer he has been with God in good conduct, the safer he will be in the operation of this knowledge. For the Spirits obey virtues.

118 Steganography

Therefore, when someone is about to approach this art, let the teacher receive him and lead him into some secret and clean place. Let the time be tranquil and serene, and the moon complete in opposition, with the sun shining clearly; and let Mercury be in the ascendant, joined to Venus or Jupiter if possible; and let Saturn and Mars be remote, because if both or either of them is with the ascendant, the instruction will not be perfect. First, he will swear this oath in the art:

I, N., swear and promise, by the power of almighty God, by the blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, by the resurrection of the dead and the last judgment, and by the salvation of my soul in the holy Catholic faith, to almighty God, to the blessed Virgin Mary, to all the Saints, and to you, N., that I will faithfully keep this art of Steganography hidden for all the days of my life, nor will I teach it to anyone without your will and consent. Moreover, by the same power I swear and promise that I will not use this knowledge against God and his commandments, nor against the holy Roman and universal Church or its ministers, nor against justice and equity. So may God help me, and so may he save me at the last judgment.

Then let the teacher read the following conjuration in the mystical language, and let him interpret it, and all the conjurations contained in this work, before the disciple, so that he may not suspect that anything diabolical, superstitious, or contrary to God, or any pact with demons, implicitly or explicitly, is in any way latently hidden there.

And after the master of this art has explained to his disciple the conjuration, order, and sequence of all the spirits, let him disclose to him the most secret mysteries of this knowledge, which have not been written and must not be written. Under the oath already sworn, he shall forbid him to reveal them to anyone as long as he lives, except to worthy persons sworn in the art, nor shall he write them down in any manner or for any reason. Then let him teach him the natures, names, places, numbers, offices, and properties of all the Spirits appointed to this art: how, when, and where one must work through them, and the remaining secrets that pertain to the perfection of this art, concerning which nothing is to be written.

140 STEGANOGRAPHY

HERE BEGINS THE THIRD BOOK OF THE STEGANOGRAPHY OF JOHANNES TRITHEMIUS, ABBOT OF SPONHEIM, TO THE MOST SERENE Prince, Lord Philipp, Count Palatine of the Rhine, Duke of Bavaria, and Prince-Elector of the Holy Empire.

PREFACE.

After, with the aid of our Lord Jesus Christ, savior of faithful souls, we completed the first two books of our art, in which I have described our Steganography as best I could, we must join this third book to them, and add things still more wonderful to wonderful aids. I found in a certain book by an ancient philosopher, who is called Menastor, that it is possible by a certain art to make known the thought of our mind to a friend, however far absent, within twenty-four hours, without words, without books, and without a messenger, most perfectly, most fully, and most secretly.

Since I was driven by an extremely strong desire to know, I began to wish to test the truth of these sayings; and after many labors I finally found the knowledge itself, proved by experience. The secret of this art is very great and wrapped in such obscurities that it is not easily accessible to anyone. For Menastor enclosed the mystery in exceedingly obscure and few words, and used such powers that it might remain secret, so that after him no one has yet been found who has dared to make his discourse clearer by any instruction. But I, fearing lest it come into the hands of the unskilled, or finally be burned in the fire, since I have now long tested it by many proofs, have wished to commit it to writing in rather clearer letters, so that, with God’s help, it may become somewhat accessible to learned men and to those most devoted to magical studies; and yet at all times remain hidden from unskilled Rapophagi, and in no way become known to their dull understanding.

Menastor said: There are seven planets, over which seven Angels preside; and subject to them are twenty-one spirits, through whom secrets are announced. Let us set out their names by means of a table. Mansion.

142 Steganography

These are the seven angels of the planets according to the tradition of the ancient sages. Each of them governs the world for 354 years and four months in his own order. Orifiel is the angel of Saturn, who from the beginning of creation governed the world for 354 years and 4 months. Afterward came Venus, then Jupiter, after him Mercury, and then Mars, afterward the Moon, and last the Sun. Each one is described as having held dominion over the world for 354 years and 4 months with his angel written for him in the common table. Thus the sages say that at the time of the Flood Samael, the angel of Mars, served in the power of rule; Gabriel, the angel of the Moon, at the time of the confusion of tongues; and Michael, the angel of the Sun, at the time of Israel’s departure from Egypt. And indeed, if anyone gives credence to the aforesaid assertion, he will easily be able by himself, from the origin of the world down to his own age, to reckon the changes of times and the government of the angels in the prescribed order. But we, pursuing those matters that are useful for our purpose, have no doubt that there are 21 other spirits subject to the aforesaid seven angels of the planets, that is, three to each one, according to the instruction of this art of ours; through them we bring about the effect of our intention. We shall observe the customary order of the planets, beginning from Saturn, the highest of all, down to the Moon: first writing out the operation of each principal angel, and then the service beneath him, and joining the chapters in order.

Chapter I.

On Orifiel, the First and Supreme Angel of Saturn, and on the operations that are performed through him.

Saturn, the planet highest and supreme of all, slow in motion by nature, cold because remote, difficult, heavy, is moved by its own natural motion from the point of its beginning 650 years to the point of its first station, remaining 30 months in any given sign, 626. Its first and supreme angel, according to the opinion of the ancients, is called Orifiel. He has under him three other principal spirits, namely Sadael, Poniel, and Morisiel, concerning whom we shall speak in their own place and order. Through this Orifiel, the great angel of Saturn, many and diverse operations are performed in Steganography. Through him we can

we can make known the secret of our mind to a friend skilled in the art, wherever he may be, by letters, if one pleases, or even without letters, and do many other wondrous things which no one else will understand if he is unskilled in this science of ours. Therefore, anyone wishing to perform some operation in Steganography through this angel, especially on the day of Saturn and in those matters, business, and causes that pertain to Saturn, must first know its various and diverse motions: namely, pure, proper, straight, retrograde, and confused. And in all these things he must know not only the general rules handed down by the astronomers, which, although they are very useful for this science of ours, nevertheless are not wholly sufficient, but also the particular rules.

Therefore, with the tables and rules concerning the motions of the planets presupposed as a foundation, which anyone working in this art must know thoroughly, we have added special rules and little tables of punctual motions throughout the individual chapters of this work; without observing them no one will be able to operate in this art. And note that the day of each planet is divided into four equal parts. The principal angel of that planet holds the first part, that is, the first three unequal hours; and his substitutes receive the remaining three parts in order.

For example: on the day of Saturn, Orifiel, its first angel, possesses the three unequal hours from sunrise, which are called planetary hours; Sadael, his first angel, possesses the second three; Poniel, the second, holds the third; and Morisiel, Orifiel’s third angel, holds the fourth three hours. Under the first three hours of the day, both of Saturn and of the other stars, one must operate in matters appropriated to Saturn through Orifiel; under the second, through Sadael; under the third, through Poniel; and under the last three, through Morisiel. And all operations, according to the motion of Saturn, receive either a prosperous effect or a weak one. But now let us set down the punctual table.

Once the mean motion of Saturn on the second day, degree, and hour has been learned from the common tables, you should know that first of all it must be carefully observed whether it is direct or retrograde; pure, proper, mixed, or confused. But you will not find this in the common tables. Therefore we have arranged the preceding table, in which you will be able to find the point of the beginning and end of its motion at any hour, with the degrees occurring together divided into particles of minutes. That is, for each minute it is to be divided into two, three, or four hourly parts, according to the proportion of pure or confused motion, that is, with the conjunction and separation of the other planets observed.

For it is impossible for you to be able to arrive at the effect of this art either through the stars or through the spirits of the stars, unless, once the punctual motion has been known and most diligently observed, you know how to order your operations precisely according to the proper qualities of the planets. For in the different degrees, signs, days, hours, minutes, seconds, and fourths of the planets, the effects, with respect to this science, vary in different ways. For in each degree we have observed and found twenty-five different changes; hence it seemed necessary to us to divide each degree into the same number of principal parts.

This division, however, does not apply through all the degrees, but only in those in which an operation is performed for signifying to absent persons everything that we wish, by the service of spirits and without letters, as we shall say. The first quarter of the day or night always serves in these things that pertain to the operation of Saturn and its beginning; the second serves for the second three hours, the third for the third, and the fourth for the fourth. Then we have set beneath this the punctual order of the motion of Saturn itself in ascending, namely when it is in one of the first four signs, which are Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer. 150 STEGANOGRAPHY

On the Varying Motion of the Planets and the Interpretation of the Tables.

Although in the present chapter a special treatment is to be given of the motions of Saturn and of his spirits, and of the operations in Steganography through them, nevertheless, lest we be forced to repeat in each chapter things once said opportunely, the studious reader must be advised to take care to remember also in the following chapters the things that we say in this chapter itself.

Now the motions of the individual planets are various, and all are most subtly divided into diverse other motions. The pure and proper motion is manifold, and is varied by very subtle divisions. Direct, retrograde, mixed, and confused motions are varied by almost as many points as they are separated from the beginning of their motion in the circle. What shall I say about finding the conjunction of the planets themselves? For, as Ptolemy says in the Centiloquium, there are one hundred twenty conjunctions among the planets themselves, namely: binary, 21; ternary, 35; quaternary, 35; quinary, 21; senary, 7; and one septenary. And we shall speak of these in their own place.

Concerning the other motions, however, although we cannot give a fixed term because of the infinite diversity by which, as points daily increase or decrease, they are varied without our knowing it, still, as fully as we have been able to observe, we have found more than 300,000 divisions, in which all the operations of this art are often varied as to their effect. And unless someone is very experienced in all these things, and knows perfectly the mean motions of the planets themselves, and then the very smallest punctual divisions, which arise from fourths, thirds, seconds, minutes, and degrees most subtly divided into equal parts, he will easily fall into true errors and will scarcely escape grave danger.

Therefore, for the perfect instruction of this science, we have arranged three tables. In the first of these, we have reduced the motion of Saturn, according to the four parts of both day and night, namely its proper and pure motion, to its punctual root, and have arranged it according to the true point of the ascendant of each sign. Beginning from the first degree of Aries, 641 points, q II and 69, we have placed the whole Zodiac in the second table

Book Three.

we have included in the table. Then, in the same second table, we have arranged the motion of Saturn in each of the twelve signs, for all the quarters of day and night, down to the minutes, so that, once we know in any hour the degree of the ascendant in which Saturn himself is, his punctual root can be clearly disclosed. Once, however, the calculation of some period has been completed, a period which I do not know whether our age can ever reach, the table must be begun again from the head of its beginning. In the third table we have reduced the sevenfold conjunction of Saturn with the other planets, which is unique, to the proportion of a point; through this all 120 conjunctions are easily reduced to the point. In the same table the pure motion of all the planets is known through the punctual division, progression, and elongation of the beginning of each, from the point in any motion, if the mean motion has first been perfectly obtained. For without knowledge of the mean motion, it is impossible for anyone to be able to approach the practice of this science. Again, even if you understand the mean motion and likewise the true motion most perfectly, it will profit you nothing for knowledge of this science unless you understand completely the three prescribed tables for all the points of the divisions in the motions of the planets, taken equally from unequal degrees, through each minute. But now let us proceed to the operation.

When all these things which we have said, and with God’s help shall say, have been known and perfectly understood, then, when you wish to operate in this most profound speculation, you must first know the rising, exaltation, and setting of all the stars of the eighth sphere through which the operation is performed, and how far each is distant from another. The stars through which we operate for announcing any secret whatever to an absent person, whether by words or by writings and without a human messenger, are seven hundred in number. Their names, places, risings, settings, elevations, distances, approaches, and recessions we have described in a special book; it would be too painstaking to repeat them here by inserting them again. Therefore, with the star observed in all respects as is proper, and with the point of the ascendant known in which Saturn is at that same hour, if the operation is performed through him, consider most diligently the quality of his motion,

whether it is direct or retrograde, pure or mixed, proper or joined with other impediments of aspects, distinct or confused. Then preserve on a clean sheet the point of the beginning of the motion in the same sign, both of Saturn himself and of the other planets conjoined with him, most subtly and properly calculated from the common tables and from those which we have set forth; and carefully observe how far it has progressed, how far it has been elevated, and how far depressed. You will do the same for the other planets conjoined with Saturn, or with that planet through which the operation is thus performed. In like manner observe most diligently by what aspect the planets behold one another, whether trine, square, conjunction, or sextile, because in these lies the greatest force of this operation. Likewise, before all things, observe in which quarter Saturn is, not only with respect to day or night, but also with respect to the sign in which he is, and with respect to the years from the beginning of the world, when he was first created in his own house; for all these things are necessary. And note that when Orifiel, the angel of Saturn, rules the world in his order, that rule will last 354 years and four months. Then every operation of this most profound science which pertains to the works of Saturn, and which is performed through him, is easy and will attain a clear effect without great labor. And the same must be observed concerning the other planets. Therefore whoever, once the principles of this art are known, wishes to operate through it without difficulty should operate through that planet whose principal angel is found by easy calculation to be governing the sphere at that time.

Therefore, when all things have been calculated most diligently and you are about to proceed to the operation, observe which angel of Saturn presides over that quarter of the day or night, and write his name together with the name of the star through which you wish to operate, which it is necessary for you to see. At any time, however, you will be able to see the stars necessary to you by the art which we have handed down, whether by day or by night. Then write on the same small sheet the other things which you know to be most secret, with the ink prepared for this according to our custom, as you know. Afterward place the very note which you have written before you upon the table, and write on another sheet the conception of your mind, what you wish the absent person to know; and roll these two notes together with one another, and place them in a higher place before you upon the table or desk. And say

Book Three

Say the conjuration appropriate to the spirit through whom you are working. Or, if you prefer to announce the secret entirely without writings, by means of a spirit or without a spirit, let it be placed at your discretion. For it is the same operation to announce a secret to a friend with a spirit or without a spirit, with a few things altered, as we shall say in its proper place. Now we shall set out the differences among the operations of Saturn and of his angels according to the four principal quarters, together with the conjurations assigned in order to each one; these are to be used when a secret is announced by means of a spirit.

On the First Angel of Saturn, Who Is the Principal One and Is Called Orifiel, Who Observes the First Quarter of Saturn

The first and principal angel of Saturn, as we have said above, is called Orifiel; together with the other angels of the planets, in his order he governs the world for 354 years and four months. He has the first part both by day and by night; and through him the operation is performed, from sunrise by day and from sunset by night up to and including the third hour, in all matters that pertain to Saturn, and on his day and night, as we have said. Therefore, when in the first quarter of Saturn you wish to announce something to an absent person without words and without letters, then no spirit of Saturn other than Orifiel is to be called by you, because through him you will be able to announce everything most perfectly.

First consider in what sign Saturn is, and in what degree, and whether he is direct or retrograde, and with which planets he is in conjunction. Let us set down an example for the first point: behold, Saturn is now in the 25th degree of Taurus, on the 28th day of the month of April in the present year, which is the year of the Lord 1500. Now therefore let us multiply 25 by 25, and they make 600. Let us divide these by four equal quarters, and 150 will remain for each quarter. Let us complete all the degrees of Saturn in the sign of Taurus, and they will be 30. Let us then multiply 30 by 25 in all, and they make 750. Let us cast off four superfluous degrees from the middle of the third quarter, and 650 will remain. Let us now take the point of Saturn’s motion from the table for the present day and the fifth hour;

and we shall be able to know what is the rising, elevation, and setting of the angel Orifiel with Saturn in the first quarter. Once these have been known, our operation will be easy.

THE THIRD BOOK.

and on the mouth the name of your absent friend, saying: This is the image of N., son of N., to whom, through Orifiel, angel of Saturn, the conception of my mind is announced. Amen. On the forehead of the image write Merion, and on the breast Troesda. Then join both images together, saying: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. Hear, Orifiel, prince of the star Saturn, and by the power of almighty God I adjure you: listen. I instruct and command you by the power of this image of yours, that you announce to N., son of N., this intention of mine (let the intention be set forth) as quickly as possible, safely, secretly, and faithfully, omitting nothing of those things which I wish him to know and which I have entrusted to you. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Then wrap those images, thus joined together, in a clean cloth washed with albisina water, and place them in a movable vessel, which the Indian sages call pharnat alronda; and cover it carefully above with shaved leather, and place it at the entrance of some closed dwelling, wherever you wish, for the space of 24 hours. Without any hesitation, your desire will be perfectly fulfilled within those 24 hours; and your absent friend will know the intention in every form most perfectly, just as you spoke it over the image, however lengthy it may have been. Whatever you wish him to know from you, he will know within those 24 hours perfectly and most secretly, so that never in eternity will any human being be able to perceive or know this without your will or that of your friend.

And it is a great secret, which none of the sages before us dared to commit to writing. But if that friend of yours wishes to know anything from you about his affairs, by means of the same spirit he can make you more certain within the same space of 24 hours, provided that he is well perfected in this art. But you, when 24 hours have elapsed, remove the images from the place in which they have been set and put them away, because at every time of Orifiel you can work through them, not only toward that friend of yours, but toward any others at all, changing only the name of that friend into the name of the person whom you wish to know something.

And note that it is not necessary for those images to be painted beautifully or elaborately; however simple they may be, it makes no difference, provided only that they have some proportionate likeness, so that they are recognized as images of human beings. But if someone wishes and is able to paint them beautifully, that neither hinders nor helps.

Once the place of the angel Sadael has been found from consideration of the fixed star at the point of Saturn's motion, make two images, in the manner we described in the preceding operation, of Orifiel, with the inscriptions, attestations, and all the other individual things that were stated there. When these have been completed, place the images themselves upon five little branches of the herb thrasnote, outside the house in a safe and secret place, and say over them: In the name of the † Father and of the † Son and of the † Holy Spirit, Amen. Just as I have placed these two images, of the angel Sadael and of N. son of N., my friend, joined together upon these five movable branches, so I command you, Sadael, by the power of Orifiel, your great prince, to bring without delay to the knowledge of the aforesaid friend the secret of my mind, which I have entrusted to you by explaining it. When these things have been said, leave the images there for 24 hours; and what you wished will be done, and your friend will know, most perfectly and secretly, everything that you said over the images. Likewise, if you wish to know concerning some absent person how he is faring, and his true condition within 24 hours, however far away he may be, you will be able to know it in this way. AND ALL THINGS THAT HAPPEN IN THE WORLD, ONCE THE CONSTELLATION HAS BEEN OBSERVED, YOU WILL BE ABLE TO KNOW THROUGH THIS ART.

On the third angel of Saturn, who is the second under Orifiel and is called Pomiel, presiding over the third quarter of Saturn.

The third angel of Saturn is called Pomiel, who is second in order under Orifiel, the principal angel of Saturn. He presides over the Saturnine seventh, eighth, and ninth hours, both by day and by night, in all things that pertain to the operation of Saturn. Since he is moved with his order toward the fixed stars 25 degrees from the East, you will find his place in this way, through the tables arranged according to his hours.
